source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus holds 44 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet, about 2.7% of Virginia's 1,603 MW of announced data center load.

The campus is three buildings, NVA1 through NVA3, and its power figure places it 12th among the 25 Virginia facilities that publish capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a typical AI training density, 44 MW implies roughly 1,100 racks. That is the physical basis for compute here: square feet and megawatts, not chips or tenants.

The certifications cover financial, healthcare, federal, and general information security standards. They show the campus is built to host regulated workloads. They say nothing about who occupies it or whether any of that capacity serves AI training rather than enterprise or cloud workloads.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, and only 25 publish power figures. Sterling is a mid-tier site within that published set. The data does not include announced expansion, tenant mix, or power utilization, so it cannot establish how much of this capacity is actually running or what it is running.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
